title: Western Blotting
author: Cynthia L. Blanco
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tpqemmw
materials: Stack gel for 30 minutes at 50 volts
Prepare 1:1 mixture of ECL reagents (Western Lighting Plus, Perkin Elmer, LLC, Massachusetts, USA)
Cover membranes with ECL for 1 minute

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization
steps.instruction: Homogenize tissue samples using a bead beater.

substeps.instruction: Fill Beadbeater tubes (BioSpec Products, Inc.) approximately ¼ full with 1mm diameter zirconia beads (BioSpec).
Add 20-25 mg of tissue and 400-500uL homogenizing buffer.
Homogenize samples using a Mini Beadbeater 16 (BioSpec) for 1 to 2 minutes.
Allow samples to rest on ice for 5-10 minutes.

steps.title: Protein Extraction and Quantification
steps.instruction: Isolate and quantify protein from the homogenate.

substeps.instruction: Transfer homogenate to clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and centrifuge at 4°C for 10 minutes at 10,000xg.
Remove the supernatant to clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and discard the pellet.
Quantify protein via spectrophotometric determination of absorbance at 280 nm using an Epoch plate reader with Take3 microplate (BioTek).
Store protein samples at -80°C.

steps.title: Gel Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run protein samples on an SDS-PAGE gel.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Mini Trans-Blot Cell with 10% agarose Mini-PROTEAN TGX precast gels (BioRad) and 1X tris/glycine/SDS running buffer (diluted from 10X in ddH20).
Fill sample volume to 15 uL with ddH20.
Heat samples for 5 minutes at 95°C.
Load samples, molecular weight marker, and controls into the prepared gel.
Run the gel for approximately 1 hour at 100-120 volts.

steps.title: Protein Transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins from the gel to a nitrocellulose membrane.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Mini Trans-Blot Cell with transfer accessories, 0.4 micron nitrocellulose membranes (BioRad), and 1X tris/glycine transfer buffer (diluted from 10X in ddH20 with 20% methanol).
Run the transfer for 1 hour at 100 volts at 4°C.

steps.title: Membrane Blocking and Primary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Block the membrane and probe with the primary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Block membranes in 10% milk/0.05% TWEEN in 1X TBS (BioRad) for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Probe membranes with primary antibody (diluted in 3% milk/0.05% TWEEN in 1X TBS) overnight at 4°C with gentle rocking.
Pour off primary antibody and wash membranes in 0.05% TWEEN/ 1X TBS 3 times for 5 minutes each.

steps.title: Secondary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Probe the membrane with the secondary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Incubate membranes in secondary antibody (diluted in 5% milk/0.05% TWEEN in 1X TBS) for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Pour off secondary antibody and wash membranes in 0.05% TWEEN/ 1X TBS 3 times for 10 minutes each.

steps.title: Imaging and Development
steps.instruction: Expose the membrane to film and develop the image.

substeps.instruction: Gently dab edges of membranes on a napkin to remove excess moisture and place into a radiography cassette.
In a dark room, place radiography film (HyBlot CL, 8 x 10 inch, Denville Scientific) into the cassette and expose to membranes for 30 seconds to 2 minutes.
Place films into a Mini-med/90 X-ray film processor (AFP imaging).
Rinse excess ECL from membranes with ddH20 after development.

steps.title: Membrane Stripping and Reprobing
steps.instruction: Strip the membrane and reprobe for the housekeeping gene.

substeps.instruction: Place membranes into Restore Plus Western Blot Stripping Buffer (Thermo-Fisher) for 7 minutes.
Rinse membranes in 0.05% TWEEN/ 1X TBS, then wash in 0.05% TWEEN/ 1X TBS for 2.5 minutes.
Block the membrane as previously described and reprobe for the housekeeping gene (GAPDH).
Place film on a clean sheet of white paper and scan as a high-resolution black and white JPEG (HP Color LaserJet Pro MFP M477fdn).
Open the image in ImageJ (NIH).
Use the rectangle tool to draw a box around the band; press Ctrl+1 to set the first row.
Move the box to the next band and press Ctrl+2; repeat until all rows/bands are selected.
Press Ctrl+3 to create plots of the rows.
Use the line tool to draw a line across the bottom of each peak.
Use the magic wand tool to quantify the area under the peak.
Copy and paste the resulting raw OD values into an Excel datasheet.

steps.title: Data Normalization and Analysis
steps.instruction: Normalize the OD values and calculate group statistics.

substeps.instruction: Divide the OD values of the protein of interest by the corresponding value of the housekeeping gene reprobe.
To normalize between gels: divide the internal control sample on gel A by the same internal control sample on gel B to obtain correction value C.
Report raw values for gel A and multiply all values in gel B by C; repeat for all gels being compared.
Calculate group means and standard deviations (or standard error) using the normalized data.

steps.title: Reagent Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare milk solutions and other reagents.

substeps.instruction: To make 3% solution: dissolve 1.5g non-fat dry milk in 50 mL TBS-Tween; fill volume to 50ml with ddH20.
To make 5% solution: dissolve 2.5g non-fat dry milk in 50 mL TBS-Tween; fill volume to 50ml with ddH20.
To make 10% solution: dissolve 5g non-fat dry milk in 50 mL TBS-Tween; fill volume to 50ml with ddH20.
Prepare 1% Bromophenol Blue: 0.1g BPB + 10ml H2O.
For pH-sensitive buffers: if pH is greater than 6.8, adjust to 6.7 with HCl; if lower, do not use.
